translationNotes.original: Hebrew: זְקֵנִים (zeqenim), elders - שַׁעַר (shaar), the gate
translationNotes.note: In the case of the stubborn son the parents do not punish him themselves. Verse 21:19 requires them to take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city at the gate, and 21:21 puts the stoning in the hands of the men of the city, not the father. The charge they must state aloud is fixed by the text: stubborn, rebellious, a glutton and a drunkard (21:20). The same elders at the same gate settle the levirate case at Deuteronomy 25:7-9.

stories.keyTakeaway: Laws are given for atoning for unsolved murders, taking captive women as wives, protecting firstborn inheritance rights, executing rebellious sons, and burying executed criminals before nightfall.

headings.text: Cursed Is Anyone Hung on a Tree

stories.title: ⚖️ Deuteronomy 22
summaryBullets: If you see your brother’s ox or sheep straying, you must not ignore it; be sure to return it to your brother. (22:1).
If your brother does not live near you, or if you do not know who he is, you are to take the animal home to remain with you until your brother comes seeking it; then you can return it to him. (22:2).
And you shall do the same for his donkey, his cloak, or anything your brother has lost and you have found. You must not ignore it. (22:3).
If you see your brother’s donkey or ox fallen on the road, you must not ignore it; you must help him lift it up. (22:4).
A woman must not wear men’s clothing, and a man must not wear women’s clothing, for whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD your God. (22:5).

If you come across a bird’s nest with chicks or eggs, either in a tree or on the ground along the road, and the mother is sitting on the chicks or eggs, you must not take the mother along with the young. (22:6).
You may take the young, but be sure to let the mother go, so that it may be well with you and that you may prolong your days. (22:7).
If you build a new house, you are to construct a railing around your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if someone falls from it. (22:8).
Do not plant your vineyard with two types of seed; if you do, the entire harvest will be defiled — both the crop you plant and the fruit of your vineyard. (22:9).
Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together. (22:10).
Do not wear clothes of wool and linen woven together. (22:11).
You are to make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear. (22:12).
Suppose a man marries a woman, has relations with her, and comes to hate her, (22:13).
and he then accuses her of shameful conduct and gives her a bad name, saying, “I married this woman and had relations with her, but I discovered she was not a virgin.” (22:14).
Then the young woman’s father and mother shall bring the proof of her virginity to the city elders at the gate (22:15).
and say to the elders, “I gave my daughter in marriage to this man, but he has come to hate her. (22:16).

And now he has accused her of shameful conduct, saying, ‘I discovered that your daughter was not a virgin.’ But here is the proof of her virginity.” And they shall spread out the cloth before the city elders. (22:17).
Then the elders of that city shall take the man and punish him. (22:18).

They are also to fine him a hundred shekels of silver and give them to the young woman’s father, because this man has given a virgin of Israel a bad name. And she shall remain his wife; he must not divorce her as long as he lives. (22:19).
If, however, this accusation is true, and no proof of the young woman’s virginity can be found, (22:20).

she shall be brought to the door of her father’s house, and there the men of her city will stone her to death. For she has committed an outrage in Israel by being promiscuous in her father’s house. So you must purge the evil from among you. (22:21).
If a man is found lying with another man’s wife, both the man who slept with her and the woman must die. You must purge the evil from Israel. (22:22).
If there is a virgin pledged in marriage to a man, and another man encounters her in the city and sleeps with her, (22:23).

you must take both of them out to the gate of that city and stone them to death— the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he has violated his neighbor’s wife. So you must purge the evil from among you. (22:24).
But if the man encounters a betrothed woman in the open country, and he overpowers her and lies with her, only the man who has done this must die. (22:25).
Do nothing to the young woman, because she has committed no sin worthy of death. This case is just like one in which a man attacks his neighbor and murders him. (22:26).
When he found her in the field, the betrothed woman cried out, but there was no one to save her. (22:27).
If a man encounters a virgin who is not pledged in marriage, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are discovered, (22:28).

then the man who lay with her must pay the young woman’s father fifty shekels of silver, and she must become his wife because he has violated her. He must not divorce her as long as he lives. (22:29).
A man is not to marry his father’s wife, so that he will not dishonor his father’s marriage bed. (22:30).
crossRefs: Exodus 22:16-17: The parallel case, where a man who seduces an unbetrothed virgin pays the bride price and the girl's father may refuse to give her to him at all, so the marriage in 22:28-29 is not forced on her house.
Numbers 15:37-41: The command to make tassels on the corners of the garment with a blue cord in each, which 22:12 repeats.
Leviticus 19:19: Do not mate two kinds of livestock, sow two kinds of seed, or wear cloth of two materials, the same rules against mixture as 22:9-11.
Exodus 23:4-5: If you come across your enemy's ox or donkey wandering off, take it back to him, the duty 22:1-4 lays on a neighbour.
Deuteronomy 24:1-4: The certificate of divorce, the exit that 22:19 and 22:29 close off to those two men for the rest of their lives.

translationNotes.note: Knotted threads at the corners of an Israelite outer garment (Numbers 15:38-39), commanded as visual reminders of God's commands. When the woman with a bleeding disorder touches the 'tassel' of Jesus' cloak (Matthew 9:20), she is grasping the most ritually charged corner of His garment.
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צִיצִת (tzitzit)

translationNotes.note: Far more than an entrance; the public square where elders heard legal cases, contracts were witnessed, market business transacted, and news was exchanged. 'Sitting in the gate' (Genesis 19:1; Ruth 4:1-11; Proverbs 31:23) signals civic authority and active community life.
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׁעַר (sha'ar)
Hebrew: מְאֹרָשָׂה (meorasah), betrothed - אֲשֶׁר לֹא־אֹרָשָׂה (asher lo orasah), 'who is not betrothed'
translationNotes.note: Betrothal in Israel was the binding half of the marriage, not an engagement a man could walk away from, and the text simply calls the woman a wife. Deuteronomy 22:24 says the offender has violated 'his neighbor's wife' though she has not yet moved into his house. That is why 22:23-27 tries her cases under the adultery rule of 22:22 while 22:28-29 handles an unbetrothed woman under a different rule entirely. The same law stands behind Matthew 1:18-19, where Joseph is called Mary's husband and needs a divorce to separate.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חָזַק (chazaq), to seize or overpower; at 22:25 וְהֶחֱזִיק־בָּהּ (vehecheziq-bah), 'and the man overpowered her'
translationNotes.note: Deuteronomy 22:25-27 is the case of force, and the verb marks it. Only the man dies. Verse 26 orders 'do nothing to the young woman, she has committed no sin worthy of death,' and then compares the crime to murder using ratsach, the same verb as 'You shall not murder' at Exodus 20:13. Verse 27 supplies the reason she is not charged: she cried out in the field and there was no one to save her. The text declares her guiltless in as many words.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תָּפַשׂ (taphas), to take hold of or catch; at 22:28 וּתְפָשָׂהּ (utephasah)
translationNotes.note: Deuteronomy 22:28-29 uses a different verb from the force case three verses earlier, and the outcome differs: the man pays the woman's father fifty shekels of silver and may never divorce her. The parallel law at Exodus 22:16-17 covers the same ground with a third verb, pathah, to entice or persuade, and there the father may refuse the marriage outright while the man still pays the bride price. Three cases, three verbs: 22:25-27 executes the man, 22:28-29 binds him, and Exodus 22:16-17 lets the father decide. The law does not use one word for all of them.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בָּעִיר (bair), in the city - בַּשָּׂדֶה (bassadeh), in the field
translationNotes.note: The setting decides the two cases. In the city (22:23-24) a cry could have been heard and answered, and both parties are charged. In the open field (22:25-27) the text states as fact that she cried and no one was there to save her, and only the man dies. The question the distinction settles is who could have heard her, and 22:27 supplies the finding a court would otherwise have to guess at.

translationNotes.term: He may never send her away
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא־יוּכַל לְשַׁלְּחָהּ כׇּל־יָמָיו (lo yukhal leshallechah kol yamav), 'he is not able to send her away all his days'
translationNotes.note: The clause falls twice in this chapter, at 22:19 on the husband who slandered his bride and again at 22:29, and both times it is a sentence passed on the man. Shillach, to send away, is the ordinary word for divorce; Deuteronomy 24:1 uses it of the man who writes the certificate and puts his wife out. Here that option is taken from him permanently, and at 22:19 he is fined a hundred shekels on top of it. The law removes a right from the man.

translationNotes.term: A hundred shekels and fifty shekels
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שֶׁקֶל (sheqel), a weight of silver
translationNotes.note: Both fines in this chapter are heavy. Leviticus 27:3-4 values a man between twenty and sixty at fifty shekels of silver for vow purposes and a woman at thirty, and Exodus 21:32 fixes thirty shekels as the sum owed an owner for a slave killed by an ox. So the fifty shekels of 22:29 matches the full valuation of a grown man, and the hundred shekels of 22:19 is double that, paid to the father of the woman whose name her husband tried to ruin.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses prescribes laws governing treatment of lost livestock, clothing restrictions, building safety, and agricultural practices; he then establishes harsh penalties for sexual misconduct including false accusations of non-virginity, adultery, and rape, with consequences varying by circumstance.

stories.title: ⚖️ Deuteronomy 23
summaryBullets: No man with crushed or severed genitals may enter the assembly of the LORD. (23:1).
No one of illegitimate birth may enter the assembly of the LORD, nor may any of his descendants, even to the tenth generation. (23:2).
No Ammonite or Moabite or any of their descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD, even to the tenth generation. (23:3).
For they did not meet you with food and water on your way out of Egypt, and they hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram-naharaim to curse you. (23:4).
Yet the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam, and the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loves you. (23:5).
You are not to seek peace or prosperity from them as long as you live. (23:6).
Do not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother. Do not despise an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land. (23:7).
The third generation of children born to them may enter the assembly of the LORD. (23:8).
When you are encamped against your enemies, then you shall keep yourself from every wicked thing. (23:9).
If any man among you becomes unclean because of a nocturnal emission, he must leave the camp and stay outside. (23:10).
When evening approaches, he must wash with water, and when the sun sets he may return to the camp. (23:11).
You must have a place outside the camp to go and relieve yourself. (23:12).
And you must have a digging tool in your equipment so that when you relieve yourself you can dig a hole and cover up your excrement. (23:13).
For the LORD your God walks throughout your camp to protect you and deliver your enemies to you. Your camp must be holy, lest He see anything unclean among you and turn away from you. (23:14).
Do not return a slave to his master if he has taken refuge with you. (23:15).
Let him live among you wherever he chooses, in the town of his pleasing. Do not oppress him. (23:16).
No daughter or son of Israel is to be a shrine prostitute. (23:17).
You must not bring the wages of a prostitute, whether female or male, into the house of the LORD your God to fulfill any vow, because both are detestable to the LORD your God. (23:18).
Do not charge your brother interest on money, food, or any other type of loan. (23:19).
You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your brother, so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything to which you put your hand in the land that you are entering to possess. (23:20).
If you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not be slow to keep it, because He will surely require it of you, and you will be guilty of sin. (23:21).
But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty of sin. (23:22).
Be careful to follow through on what comes from your lips, because you have freely vowed to the LORD your God with your own mouth. (23:23).
When you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat your fill of grapes, but you must not put any in your basket. (23:24).
When you enter your neighbor’s grainfield, you may pluck the heads of grain with your hand, but you must not put a sickle to your neighbor’s grain. (23:25).
crossRefs: Numbers 22:1-6: Balak of Moab sends for Balaam to curse Israel, the reason given in 23:4.
Nehemiah 13:1-3: This law is read aloud, and everyone of foreign descent is separated from Israel.
Ruth 4:13-17: Ruth the Moabitess bears Obed, the grandfather of David.
Isaiah 56:3-5: The eunuch who keeps the covenant is given a name in God's house better than sons and daughters.
Exodus 22:25: Do not act as a creditor or charge interest to a poor man among My people.

translationNotes.term: Do not hand back a runaway slave
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא־תַסְגִּיר עֶבֶד אֶל־אֲדֹנָיו (lo tasgir eved el-adonav), 'you shall not hand over a slave to his master'
translationNotes.note: Deuteronomy 23:15-16 forbids returning an escaped slave, orders that he be allowed to settle in whatever town he chooses, and adds 'do not oppress him.' Every other surviving law code of the region runs the opposite way. The laws of Hammurabi of Babylon, carved about 1750 BC and now in the Louvre, make it a capital offence to bring a slave out through the city gates (law 15) or to shelter a runaway and refuse to surrender him when the officer demands it (law 16), and law 17 pays a two-shekel reward to anyone who catches one and brings him back. The Torah offers no reward and orders no return.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קְהַל יְהוָה (qehal YHWH), the assembly of the LORD
translationNotes.note: The qahal is Israel gathered as a congregation, not the population at large and not the land. Exclusion at 23:1-8 removed a man from that standing; it did not put him outside Israel. The same passage admits Edomites and Egyptians in the third generation and gives the reasons, Edom is your brother and you lived as a foreigner in Egypt (23:7-8). Isaiah 56:3-5 takes up the eunuch of 23:1 by name and promises him a memorial in God's house better than sons and daughters.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מוֹאָב (Moav) - בֶּן־עַמִּי (Ben-Ammi), 'son of my kin'
translationNotes.note: Both nations descend from Lot by his daughters after Sodom, and Genesis 19:37-38 records the names given to the two sons. They held the plateau and the deep valleys east of the Dead Sea, on Israel's approach route from the wilderness. Deuteronomy 23:4 states the charge against them: they met Israel with no food or water, and they hired Balaam of Pethor to curse them (Numbers 22:1-6). Ruth 4:13-17 then has a Moabite woman become great-grandmother to David.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קְדֵשָׁה (qedeshah), female - קָדֵשׁ (qadesh), male
translationNotes.note: Both words are built on the root for holy, so these were people formally attached to a sanctuary rather than street traders, and 23:17 forbids Israel to supply either. Genesis 38:21-22 uses qedeshah of the woman Judah's friend goes back to look for. 1 Kings 14:24 reports the qadesh present in the land under Rehoboam, and 15:12 has Asa driving them out. Hosea 4:14 charges the men of Israel with sacrificing alongside such women.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה (etnan zonah), 'the hire of a harlot' - מְחִיר כֶּלֶב (mechir kelev), 'the price of a dog'
translationNotes.note: Where English versions of 23:18 read 'male prostitute,' the Hebrew word is dog. The verse refuses both payments as an offering in the house of the LORD for any vow, and calls both detestable to Him. Micah 1:7 uses etnan the same way, of harlot's wages gathered into an idol and burned back out of it.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נֶשֶׁךְ (neshekh), 'a bite,' from נָשַׁךְ (nashakh), to bite
translationNotes.note: The noun for interest is built on the verb to bite, and 23:19 uses both, closing with 'anything that may be lent for interest' in the verb form. The ban covers money, food, and anything else, and it runs toward a brother Israelite; 23:20 permits interest toward a foreigner. Exodus 22:25 and Leviticus 25:36-37 state the same rule, and Leviticus pairs it with a second word, tarbit, increase.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קָמָה (qamah), standing grain - חֶרְמֵשׁ (chermesh), a sickle
translationNotes.note: Deuteronomy 23:24-25 lets any passer-by eat his fill of a neighbor's grapes or pull heads of grain by hand, and draws the line at the container and the tool: no basket, no sickle. That marks off a traveler's meal from a harvest. It is the law the disciples are keeping at Matthew 12:1 when they pluck heads of grain crossing the fields, which is why the objection raised against them is about the sabbath and not about theft.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses lists who cannot enter the LORD's assembly - including the emasculated, those born of forbidden marriages, Ammonites, and Moabites - while permitting Edomites and Egyptians after certain generations. He then instructs the people on camp purity, treatment of refugees, prohibitions on prostitution and interest-charging, proper vow-keeping, and gleaning rights in neighbors' fields.

stories.title: ⚖️ Deuteronomy 24
summaryBullets: If a man marries a woman, but she becomes displeasing to him because he finds some indecency in her, he may write her a certificate of divorce, hand it to her, and send her away from his house. (24:1).
If, after leaving his house, she goes and becomes another man’s wife, (24:2).
and the second man hates her, writes her a certificate of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house, or if he dies, (24:3).

then the husband who divorced her first may not remarry her after she has been defiled, for that is an abomination to the LORD. You must not bring sin upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance. (24:4).
If a man is newly married, he must not be sent to war or be pressed into any duty. For one year he is free to stay at home and bring joy to the wife he has married. (24:5).
Do not take a pair of millstones or even an upper millstone as security for a debt, because that would be taking one’s livelihood as security. (24:6).
If a man is caught kidnapping one of his Israelite brothers, whether he treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must die. So you must purge the evil from among you. (24:7).
In cases of infectious skin diseases, be careful to diligently follow everything the Levitical priests instruct you. Be careful to do as I have commanded them. (24:8).
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the journey after you came out of Egypt. (24:9).
When you lend anything to your neighbor, do not enter his house to collect security. (24:10).
You are to stand outside while the man to whom you are lending brings the security out to you. (24:11).
If he is a poor man, you must not go to sleep with the security in your possession; (24:12).
be sure to return it to him by sunset, so that he may sleep in his own cloak and bless you, and this will be credited to you as righteousness before the LORD your God. (24:13).
Do not oppress a hired hand who is poor and needy, whether he is a brother or a foreigner residing in one of your towns. (24:14).
You are to pay his wages each day before sunset, because he is poor and depends on them. Otherwise he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin. (24:15).
Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin. (24:16).
Do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless, and do not take a widow’s cloak as security. (24:17).
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from that place. Therefore I am commanding you to do this. (24:18).

If you are harvesting in your field and forget a sheaf there, do not go back to get it. It is to be left for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands. (24:19).
When you beat the olives from your trees, you must not go over the branches again. What remains will be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow. (24:20).
When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you must not go over the vines again. What remains will be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow. (24:21).
Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. Therefore I am commanding you to do this. (24:22).
crossRefs: Matthew 19:7-9: The Pharisees ask why Moses commanded a certificate of divorce, and Jesus answers that it was for hardness of heart.
Leviticus 19:9-10: Do not reap to the very edges of your field, and leave the fallen grain for the poor and the foreigner.
Ruth 2:2-17: Ruth gleans behind the harvesters in the field of Boaz, who tells his men to leave grain for her.
Exodus 22:26-27: Return a neighbor's cloak taken in pledge before sunset, for it is his only covering.
James 5:4: The wages of the harvesters, held back by fraud, cry out against the rich.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת (sefer keritut), Greek: βιβλίον ἀποστασίου (biblion apostasíou), Aramaic: ספר כריתות (sefer keritut)
translationNotes.note: Legal document releasing a wife; regulated but not commanded.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא יוּמְתוּ אָבוֹת עַל בָּנִים… אִישׁ בְּחֶטְאוֹ יוּמָתוּ, Greek (LXX): οὐ θανατωθήσονται πατέρες ἐπὶ τέκνοις… ἕκαστος ἐπὶ τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ αὐτοῦ, Aramaic: לָא יִתְקְטְלוּ אָבוֹהִי־עַל בְּנִין… גְּבַר עַל חוֹבֵיהּ יִתְקְטֵל
translationNotes.note: No executing family members for another person’s crime.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֶרְוַת דָּבָר (ervat davar), 'the nakedness of a thing'
translationNotes.note: The ground for divorce at 24:1 is two words the chapter never defines, and the same pair stands at Deuteronomy 23:14 for something unclean found in the camp. Whatever it covers, 24:1-4 does not command divorce or approve it; it takes a man who has already done it and issues one rule, at 24:4, that the first husband may not take her back after a second marriage. When the Pharisees put this passage to Jesus at Matthew 19:3-9, He answers that Moses permitted it for hardness of heart and that from the beginning it was not so.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גֹּנֵב נֶפֶשׁ (gonev nefesh), 'one who steals a soul' - Greek: ἀνδραποδιστής (andrapodistes), a slaver
translationNotes.note: Deuteronomy 24:7 sentences to death anyone who steals a fellow Israelite and either treats him as goods or sells him, and Exodus 21:16 says the same of stealing any man, whether he has already sold him or still holds him. Taking the person is itself the capital crime, so the law outlaws the supply end of the slave trade rather than regulating it. Genesis 37:26-28 is the case in the narrative: Joseph sold to a passing caravan for twenty pieces of silver. Paul drops the Greek word for that trade into his list at 1 Timothy 1:10.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בְּיוֹמוֹ תִתֵּן שְׂכָרוֹ (beyomo titten sekharo), 'in his day you shall give his wage' - נֹשֵׂא אֶת־נַפְשׁוֹ (nose et nafsho), 'he lifts up his soul to it'
translationNotes.note: A day laborer kept no reserve, so 24:15 requires payment the same day before the sun goes down, and gives the reason in an idiom English flattens: he is poor, and he lifts up his soul to that wage. The rule protects the foreigner working in your towns as well as the brother (24:14). Leviticus 19:13 states it as a ban on holding a hired man's pay overnight until morning. James 5:4 says the wages held back by fraud are crying out, and that the cries have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֹמֶר (omer), a sheaf
translationNotes.note: Deuteronomy 24:19-21 adds a fourth harvest right to the three in Leviticus 19:9-10: the sheaf you left in the field is not yours to go back for, and neither is a second pass over the olive branches or the vines. The owner is forbidden to be thorough, and what he misses belongs to the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow. Ruth 2 shows the system running, with Ruth working behind the reapers in the field of Boaz. The passage gives the same reason twice: you were slaves in Egypt (24:18, 24:22).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רֵחַיִם וָרָכֶב (rechayim varakhev), 'a pair of millstones and the upper stone'
translationNotes.note: Grain was ground at home each day between two stones, the lower one fixed and the upper one turned by hand, so a household without them could not eat. Deuteronomy 24:6 bars taking either stone as security for a debt and says why in four Hebrew words: he is taking a life in pledge. The same chapter bars entering a debtor's house to seize the pledge (24:10-11) and bars keeping a poor man's cloak overnight (24:12-13), which Exodus 22:26-27 also commands.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses establishes laws on divorce, military exemptions for newlyweds, pledges for debts, kidnapping, skin diseases, lending practices, worker wages, and leaving harvest gleanings for foreigners, the fatherless, and widows.

stories.title: ⚖️ Deuteronomy 25
summaryBullets: If there is a dispute between men, they are to go to court to be judged, so that the innocent may be acquitted and the guilty condemned. (25:1).
If the guilty man deserves to be beaten, the judge shall have him lie down and be flogged in his presence with the number of lashes his crime warrants. (25:2).
He may receive no more than forty lashes, lest your brother be beaten any more than that and be degraded in your sight. (25:3).
Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain. (25:4).

When brothers dwell together and one of them dies without a son, the widow must not marry outside the family. Her husband’s brother is to take her as his wife and fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law for her. (25:5).
The first son she bears will carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name will not be blotted out from Israel. (25:6).

But if the man does not want to marry his brother’s widow, she is to go to the elders at the city gate and say, “My husband’s brother refuses to preserve his brother’s name in Israel. He is not willing to perform the duty of a brother-in-law for me.” (25:7).
Then the elders of his city shall summon him and speak with him. If he persists and says, “I do not want to marry her,” (25:8).

his brother’s widow shall go up to him in the presence of the elders, remove his sandal, spit in his face, and declare, “This is what is done to the man who will not maintain his brother’s line.” (25:9).
And his family name in Israel will be called “The House of the Unsandaled.” (25:10).
If two men are fighting, and the wife of one comes to rescue her husband from the one striking him, and she reaches out her hand and grabs his genitals, (25:11).
you are to cut off her hand. You must show her no pity. (25:12).
You shall not have two differing weights in your bag, one heavy and one light. (25:13).
You shall not have two differing measures in your house, one large and one small. (25:14).
You must maintain accurate and honest weights and measures, so that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you. (25:15).
For everyone who behaves dishonestly in regard to these things is detestable to the LORD your God. (25:16).
Remember what the Amalekites did to you along your way from Egypt, (25:17).
how they met you on your journey when you were tired and weary, and they attacked all your stragglers; they had no fear of God. (25:18).

When the LORD your God gives you rest from the enemies around you in the land that He is giving you to possess as an inheritance, you are to blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget! (25:19).
crossRefs: Genesis 38:6-11: Onan refuses to raise up offspring for his dead brother, and the LORD puts him to death.
Ruth 4:1-10: The nearer kinsman takes off his sandal at the gate, and Boaz redeems the field and marries Ruth.
2 Corinthians 11:24: Five times Paul received from the Jews forty lashes minus one.
1 Corinthians 9:9: Paul cites 'Do not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain'.
1 Samuel 15:1-3: Saul is sent against Amalek for what Amalek did to Israel on the way up from Egypt.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יָבָם (yavam), a husband's brother - Latin: levir, brother-in-law
translationNotes.note: If a man died with no son, his brother was to marry the widow and the first son she bore counted as the dead man's heir, so that the family name and its land stayed together (25:5-6). The English name comes from the Latin word for brother-in-law. A brother who refused was taken to the gate, had his sandal pulled off by the widow, was spat at, and his household carried the name The House of the Unsandaled from then on. Genesis 38 turns on this duty, Ruth 4:7-8 uses the sandal as the legal token, and the Sadducees build their question to Jesus on it at Matthew 22:24-28.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אַרְבָּעִים (arbaim), forty
translationNotes.note: Deuteronomy 25:3 caps a flogging at forty and gives the reason: beyond that a man is degraded in the sight of his own people. Later Jewish practice fixed the count at thirty-nine so that a miscount could never break the law, a rule set down in the Mishnah at Makkot 3:10. That is why Paul reports receiving from the Jews five times the forty lashes minus one, at 2 Corinthians 11:24.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא־תַחְסֹם שׁוֹר בְּדִישׁוֹ (lo-tachsom shor be-disho)
translationNotes.note: Grain was threshed by driving oxen over the cut stalks on a hard floor, often dragging a weighted sledge, and a muzzle would stop the animal snatching mouthfuls as it worked. Verse 25:4 forbids the muzzle, so the animal eats while it labours. Paul quotes the line twice for the support of those who work in the gospel, at 1 Corinthians 9:9 and 1 Timothy 5:18.

translationNotes.term: two differing weights in your bag
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֶבֶן וָאָבֶן (even va-aven), literally 'a stone and a stone'
translationNotes.note: Weights were literally stones carried in a pouch and set against goods on a balance, so a trader with a heavy stone for buying and a light one for selling could cheat in both directions. Verses 25:13-16 ban the practice outright and call it detestable to the LORD. Inscribed stone weights of this kind have been excavated across Israel, including the beka weight found in Jerusalem; Proverbs 11:1 and 20:23 and Amos 8:5 all take up the same complaint.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֲמָלֵק (Amaleq) - נֶחֱשָׁלִים (nechshalim), those lagging behind
translationNotes.note: Verses 25:17-19 supply the detail Exodus 17:8-16 leaves out: Amalek attacked the ones at the back, when Israel was tired and worn out. They were a desert people descended from Esau through Eliphaz (Genesis 36:12), so this is a related nation. Saul loses the kingdom over sparing their king Agag at 1 Samuel 15, and Haman, who tries to destroy the whole Jewish people, is introduced as the Agagite at Esther 3:1.

stories.keyTakeaway: Courts will judge disputes and limit flogging to forty lashes; widows of childless brothers must marry the brother-in-law unless he refuses and is publicly shamed; honest weights and measures are required; Israel must remember the Amalekites' ambush in the wilderness and eliminate them once settled in the land.

stories.title: ⚖️ Deuteronomy 26
summaryBullets: When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you take possession of it and settle in it, (26:1).

you are to take some of the firstfruits of all your produce from the soil of the land that the LORD your God is giving you and put them in a basket. Then go to the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for His Name, (26:2).
to the priest who is serving at that time, and say to him, “I declare today to the LORD your God that I have entered the land that the LORD swore to our fathers to give us.” (26:3).
Then the priest shall take the basket from your hands and place it before the altar of the LORD your God, (26:4).
and you are to declare before the LORD your God, “My father was a wandering Aramean, and he went down to Egypt few in number and lived there and became a great nation, mighty and numerous. (26:5).
But the Egyptians mistreated us and afflicted us, putting us to hard labor. (26:6).
So we called out to the LORD, the God of our fathers; and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, toil, and oppression. (26:7).
Then the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, signs, and wonders. (26:8).
And He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey. (26:9).
And now, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the land that You, O LORD, have given me.” Then you are to place the basket before the LORD your God and bow down before Him. (26:10).
So you shall rejoice — you, the Levite, and the foreigner dwelling among you — in all the good things the LORD your God has given to you and your household. (26:11).

When you have finished laying aside a tenth of all your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, you are to give it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, that they may eat and be filled within your gates. (26:12).

Then you shall declare in the presence of the LORD your God, “I have removed from my house the sacred portion and have given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, according to all the commandments You have given me. I have not transgressed or forgotten Your commandments. (26:13).

I have not eaten any of the sacred portion while in mourning, or removed any of it while unclean, or offered any of it for the dead. I have obeyed the LORD my God; I have done everything You commanded me. (26:14).
Look down from Your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel and the land You have given us as You swore to our fathers— a land flowing with milk and honey.” (26:15).
The LORD your God commands you this day to follow these statutes and ordinances. You must be careful to follow them with all your heart and with all your soul. (26:16).
Today you have proclaimed that the LORD is your God and that you will walk in His ways, keep His statutes and commandments and ordinances, and listen to His voice. (26:17).
And today the LORD has proclaimed that you are His people and treasured possession as He promised, that you are to keep all His commandments, (26:18).
that He will set you high in praise and name and honor above all the nations He has made, and that you will be a holy people to the LORD your God, as He has promised. (26:19).
crossRefs: Exodus 23:19: Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God.
Leviticus 23:9-14: The sheaf of firstfruits is waved before the LORD, and no new grain is eaten until it is brought.
Deuteronomy 14:28-29: Every third year the tithe is stored in your towns for the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
Genesis 46:1-7: Jacob goes down into Egypt with his whole household, the descent rehearsed in the creed of 26:5.
Nehemiah 10:35-37: The people bind themselves by oath to bring the firstfruits and the tithes to the house of God.

translationNotes.note: The first portion of each harvest offered to God before the rest could be eaten (Exodus 23:19; Leviticus 23:9-14). Paul calls the resurrected Christ 'the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep' (1 Corinthians 15:20); the guarantee that the full resurrection harvest will follow.
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בִּכּוּרִים (bikkurim)

translationNotes.note: A male descendant of Levi (excluding the Aaronic priestly line). Assisted the priests in temple service: music, gatekeeping, instructing the people, preparing sacrifices. The priest and Levite who pass by the wounded man in the Good Samaritan parable (Luke 10:31-32) make Jesus' point cut sharper; both were professionally obligated to help.
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֵוִי (lewi)

translationNotes.term: My father was a wandering Aramean
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֲרַמִּי אֹבֵד אָבִי (arami oved avi)
translationNotes.note: The confession recited over the firstfruits basket at 26:5-10 is the shortest summary of Israel's history in the Bible: an ancestor with no land, a descent into Egypt, slavery, a cry, a rescue, and this basket of produce as proof of the land. The Aramean is Jacob, whose mother's family lived at Paddan-aram and who spent twenty years there with Laban (Genesis 29-31). Oved means perishing or lost, a man without a settled place.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׁנַת הַמַּעֲשֵׂר (shenat ha-maaser), the year of the tithe
translationNotes.note: Every third year the tenth stayed in the town instead of going to the sanctuary, and 26:12 names who it went to: the Levite, the resident foreigner, the fatherless and the widow, so that they may eat within your gates and be satisfied. Deuteronomy 14:28-29 gives the same rule. Verses 26:13-14 then require a declaration in God's presence that it was handed over in full, which makes the giver answerable for it out loud.

stories.keyTakeaway: When you settle in the land, bring firstfruits to the priest at God's chosen place and recite how God brought you out of Egypt; in the third year, give a tenth of your produce to Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows, then declare before God that you have obeyed his commands.

stories.title: ⛰️ Deuteronomy 27
summaryBullets: Then Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people: “Keep all the commandments I am giving you today. (27:1).
And on the day you cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, set up large stones and coat them with plaster. (27:2).

Write on them all the words of this law when you have crossed over to enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised you. (27:3).
And when you have crossed the Jordan, you are to set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I am commanding you today, and you are to coat them with plaster. (27:4).
Moreover, you are to build there an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. You must not use any iron tool on them. (27:5).
You shall build the altar of the LORD your God with uncut stones and offer upon it burnt offerings to the LORD your God. (27:6).
There you are to sacrifice your peace offerings, eating them and rejoicing in the presence of the LORD your God. (27:7).
And you shall write distinctly upon these stones all the words of this law.” (27:8).
Then Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel: “Be silent, O Israel, and listen! This day you have become the people of the LORD your God. (27:9).
You shall therefore obey the voice of the LORD your God and follow His commandments and statutes I am giving you today.” (27:10).
On that day Moses commanded the people: (27:11).
“When you have crossed the Jordan, these tribes shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin. (27:12).
And these tribes shall stand on Mount Ebal to deliver the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali. (27:13).
Then the Levites shall proclaim in a loud voice to every Israelite: (27:14).
‘Cursed is the man who makes a carved idol or molten image — an abomination to the LORD, the work of the hands of a craftsman — and sets it up in secret.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:15).
‘Cursed is he who dishonors his father or mother.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:16).
‘Cursed is he who moves his neighbor’s boundary stone.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:17).
‘Cursed is he who lets a blind man wander in the road.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:18).
‘Cursed is he who withholds justice from the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:19).
‘Cursed is he who sleeps with his father’s wife, for he has violated his father’s marriage bed.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:20).
‘Cursed is he who lies with any animal.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:21).
‘Cursed is he who sleeps with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:22).
‘Cursed is he who sleeps with his mother-in-law.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:23).
‘Cursed is he who strikes down his neighbor in secret.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:24).
‘Cursed is he who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:25).
‘Cursed is he who does not put the words of this law into practice.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ (27:26).
crossRefs: Joshua 8:30-35: Joshua builds the altar on Mount Ebal, writes a copy of the law on the stones, and reads the blessings and curses.
Deuteronomy 11:29: The blessing is set on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Exodus 20:24-25: An altar of earth or of uncut stone; a tool laid on the stone profanes it.
Galatians 3:10: Cursed is everyone who does not continue in everything written in the Book of the Law, quoting 27:26.
Nehemiah 8:1-8: Ezra reads the Book of the Law aloud from daybreak, and the people answer, Amen, Amen.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָרַר (ʾārar), Greek: καταράομαι (kataraomai), Aramaic: ארר (arar)
translationNotes.note: Invocation of divine judgment on disobedience; contrasted with blessing.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שִׂיד (sid, 'lime plaster')
translationNotes.note: Not carving. Lime plaster was skimmed over rough stone to make a white writing surface, and the text was then painted on in ink, which is far faster than chiseling a long document. The technique is attested in the region: the inscription found in 1967 at Deir Alla in Jordan, dated to about 800 BC, is a long text written in black and red ink on wall plaster, and it names Balaam son of Beor.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הַר גְּרִזִים (Har Gerizim) - הַר עֵיבָל (Har Eival)
translationNotes.note: Two summits facing each other across the valley of Shechem in the middle of the country, Ebal on the north at about 3,070 feet and Gerizim on the south at about 2,890 feet. The valley floor between them is narrow, and the facing slopes form a natural amphitheater in which a voice from one side carries to the other. The ceremony puts six tribes on each slope with the ark and the Levites in the gap between.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָמֵן (amen)
translationNotes.note: From the root aman, to be firm, steady, reliable. Said in answer to an oath it means 'let it stand, and let it stand against me', so each of the twelve responses in this chapter makes the whole assembly a consenting party to the curse. It is a legal act of ratification, not a devotional word.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גְּבוּל (gevul, 'border, boundary marker')
translationNotes.note: Fields were marked by set stones, and moving one at night stole land in a way no witness could see, which is why the law answers it with a curse instead of a court case. The same practice is protected across the region: Mesopotamian estates were recorded on carved boundary stones, kudurru, that carried curses on anyone who shifted or defaced them.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses instructs Israel to set up plastered stones inscribed with the law on Mount Ebal after crossing the Jordan, build an altar there, and then arrange for six tribes to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless while six others stand on Mount Ebal to recite curses for violations of the covenant.

stories.title: ⛰️ Deuteronomy 28
summaryBullets: “Now if you faithfully obey the voice of the LORD your God and are careful to follow all His commandments I am giving you today, the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth. (28:1).
And all these blessings will come upon you and overtake you, if you will obey the voice of the LORD your God: (28:2).
You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the country. (28:3).
The fruit of your womb will be blessed, as well as the produce of your land and the offspring of your livestock — the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks. (28:4).
Your basket and kneading bowl will be blessed. (28:5).
You will be blessed when you come in and blessed when you go out. (28:6).
The LORD will cause the enemies who rise up against you to be defeated before you. They will march out against you in one direction but flee from you in seven. (28:7).
The LORD will decree a blessing on your barns and on everything to which you put your hand; the LORD your God will bless you in the land He is giving you. (28:8).
The LORD will establish you as His holy people, just as He has sworn to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in His ways. (28:9).
Then all the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they will stand in awe of you. (28:10).

The LORD will make you prosper abundantly — in the fruit of your womb, the offspring of your livestock, and the produce of your land — in the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give you. (28:11).
The LORD will open the heavens, His abundant storehouse, to send rain on your land in season and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations, but borrow from none. (28:12).

The LORD will make you the head and not the tail; you will only move upward and never downward, if you hear and carefully follow the commandments of the LORD your God, which I am giving you today. (28:13).
Do not turn aside to the right or to the left from any of the words I command you today, and do not go after other gods to serve them. (28:14).
If, however, you do not obey the LORD your God by carefully following all His commandments and statutes I am giving you today, all these curses will come upon you and overtake you: (28:15).
You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the country. (28:16).
Your basket and kneading bowl will be cursed. (28:17).
The fruit of your womb will be cursed, as well as the produce of your land, the calves of your herds, and the lambs of your flocks. (28:18).
You will be cursed when you come in and cursed when you go out. (28:19).

The LORD will send curses upon you, confusion and reproof in all to which you put your hand, until you are destroyed and quickly perish because of the wickedness you have committed in forsaking Him. (28:20).
The LORD will make the plague cling to you until He has exterminated you from the land that you are entering to possess. (28:21).
The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, with fever and inflammation, with scorching heat and drought, and with blight and mildew; these will pursue you until you perish. (28:22).
The sky over your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron. (28:23).
The LORD will turn the rain of your land into dust and powder; it will descend on you from the sky until you are destroyed. (28:24).

The LORD will cause you to be defeated before your enemies. You will march out against them in one direction but flee from them in seven. You will be an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth. (28:25).
Your corpses will be food for all the birds of the air and beasts of the earth, with no one to scare them away. (28:26).
The LORD will afflict you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors and scabs and itch from which you cannot be cured. (28:27).
The LORD will afflict you with madness, blindness, and confusion of mind, (28:28).
and at noon you will grope about like a blind man in the darkness. You will not prosper in your ways. Day after day you will be oppressed and plundered, with no one to save you. (28:29).
You will be pledged in marriage to a woman, but another man will violate her. You will build a house but will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard but will not enjoy its fruit. (28:30).

Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, but you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be taken away and not returned to you. Your flock will be given to your enemies, and no one will save you. (28:31).
Your sons and daughters will be given to another nation, while your eyes grow weary looking for them day after day, with no power in your hand. (28:32).
A people you do not know will eat the produce of your land and of all your toil. All your days you will be oppressed and crushed. (28:33).
You will be driven mad by the sights you see. (28:34).
The LORD will afflict you with painful, incurable boils on your knees and thighs, from the soles of your feet to the top of your head. (28:35).
The LORD will bring you and the king you appoint to a nation neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you will worship other gods— gods of wood and stone. (28:36).
You will become an object of horror, scorn, and ridicule among all the nations to which the LORD will drive you. (28:37).
You will sow much seed in the field but harvest little, because the locusts will consume it. (28:38).
You will plant and cultivate vineyards, but will neither drink the wine nor gather the grapes, because worms will eat them. (28:39).
You will have olive trees throughout your territory but will never anoint yourself with oil, because the olives will drop off. (28:40).
You will father sons and daughters, but they will not remain yours, because they will go into captivity. (28:41).
Swarms of locusts will consume all your trees and the produce of your land. (28:42).
The foreigner living among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you sink down lower and lower. (28:43).
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail. (28:44).

All these curses will come upon you. They will pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, since you did not obey the LORD your God and keep the commandments and statutes He gave you. (28:45).
These curses will be a sign and a wonder upon you and your descendants forever. (28:46).
Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart in all your abundance, (28:47).
you will serve your enemies the LORD will send against you in famine, thirst, nakedness, and destitution. He will place an iron yoke on your neck until He has destroyed you. (28:48).
The LORD will bring a nation from afar, from the ends of the earth, to swoop down upon you like an eagle — a nation whose language you will not understand, (28:49).
a ruthless nation with no respect for the old and no pity for the young. (28:50).

They will eat the offspring of your livestock and the produce of your land until you are destroyed. They will leave you no grain or new wine or oil, no calves of your herds or lambs of your flocks, until they have caused you to perish. (28:51).

They will besiege all the cities throughout your land, until the high and fortified walls in which you trust have fallen. They will besiege all your cities throughout the land that the LORD your God has given you. (28:52).
Then you will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of the sons and daughters whom the LORD your God has given you, in the siege and distress that your enemy will inflict on you. (28:53).
The most gentle and refined man among you will begrudge his brother, the wife he embraces, and the rest of his children who have survived, (28:54).
refusing to share with any of them the flesh of his children he will eat because he has nothing left in the siege and distress that your enemy will inflict on you within all your gates. (28:55).

The most gentle and refined woman among you, so gentle and refined she would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground, will begrudge the husband she embraces and her son and daughter (28:56).

the afterbirth that comes from between her legs and the children she bears, because she will secretly eat them for lack of anything else in the siege and distress that your enemy will inflict on you within your gates. (28:57).
If you are not careful to observe all the words of this law which are written in this book, that you may fear this glorious and awesome name— the LORD your God— (28:58).
He will bring upon you and your descendants extraordinary disasters, severe and lasting plagues, and terrible and chronic sicknesses. (28:59).
He will afflict you again with all the diseases you dreaded in Egypt, and they will cling to you. (28:60).
The LORD will also bring upon you every sickness and plague not recorded in this Book of the Law, until you are destroyed. (28:61).
You who were as numerous as the stars in the sky will be left few in number, because you would not obey the voice of the LORD your God. (28:62).

Just as it pleased the LORD to make you prosper and multiply, so also it will please Him to annihilate you and destroy you. And you will be uprooted from the land you are entering to possess. (28:63).

Then the LORD will scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you will worship other gods, gods of wood and stone, which neither you nor your fathers have known. (28:64).
Among those nations you will find no repose, not even a resting place for the sole of your foot. There the LORD will give you a trembling heart, failing eyes, and a despairing soul. (28:65).
So your life will hang in doubt before you, and you will be afraid night and day, never certain of survival. (28:66).

In the morning you will say, ‘If only it were evening!’ and in the evening you will say, ‘If only it were morning!’— because of the dread in your hearts of the terrifying sights you will see. (28:67).

The LORD will return you to Egypt in ships by a route that I said you should never see again. There you will sell yourselves to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one will buy you.” (28:68).
crossRefs: Leviticus 26:14-39: The earlier list of escalating punishments for a people who will not listen.
2 Kings 25:1-12: Jerusalem is besieged until famine, the wall is broken through, and the people are carried away.
Lamentations 4:9-10: Compassionate women boiled their own children when the daughter of my people was destroyed.
Daniel 9:11-13: Daniel says the curse and the sworn judgment written in the Law of Moses have been poured out on us.
Nehemiah 9:32-37: The returned people confess that they are slaves in the land God gave their fathers.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָרַר (ʾārar), Greek: καταράομαι (kataraomai), Aramaic: ארר (arar)
translationNotes.note: Invocation of divine judgment on disobedience; contrasted with blessing.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בְּרָכָה (berakhah) - קְלָלָה (qelalah)
translationNotes.note: Fourteen verses of blessing and fifty-four of curse. That imbalance is not an accident of mood; it is the shape of the treaty documents of the ancient Near East, where the curse section is always the long one because the curses are the enforcement clause. The blessings say what the relationship gives; the curses say what breaking it costs, in detail, so that no party can claim he was not told.

translationNotes.term: The sky over your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שָׁמֶיךָ נְחֹשֶׁת ... הָאָרֶץ בַּרְזֶל (shameykha nechoshet ... ha-arets barzel)
translationNotes.note: A drought curse in metal. A sky of bronze lets no rain through; ground of iron takes no plow and grows nothing. Leviticus 26:19 states the same picture with the two metals swapped. The image belongs to the standard curse vocabulary of ancient treaties, where the gods of both parties were called on to shut the sky and harden the ground against a covenant breaker.

translationNotes.term: An iron yoke on your neck
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֹל בַּרְזֶל (ol barzel)
translationNotes.note: The yoke is the standard image for vassalage, taken from the beam laid across a plow team's necks. Jeremiah acted it out, wearing a wooden yoke through Jerusalem until Hananiah broke it, and the word came back that the wooden yoke would be replaced with iron (Jeremiah 27:2, 28:13). Iron means a subjection that cannot be shrugged off.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses presents the blessings Israel will receive for full obedience to God's commands, then details the extensive curses that will follow disobedience, including disease, military defeat, crop failure, exile, and enslavement.

stories.title: ⛰️ Deuteronomy 29
summaryBullets: These are the words of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant He had made with them at Horeb. (29:1).
Moses summoned all Israel and proclaimed to them, “You have seen with your own eyes everything the LORD did in Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his officials, and to all his land. (29:2).
You saw with your own eyes the great trials, and those miraculous signs and wonders. (29:3).
Yet to this day the LORD has not given you a mind to understand, eyes to see, or ears to hear. (29:4).
For forty years I led you in the wilderness, yet your clothes and sandals did not wear out. (29:5).
You ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am the LORD your God. (29:6).
When you reached this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against us in battle, but we defeated them. (29:7).
We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. (29:8).
So keep and follow the words of this covenant, that you may prosper in all you do. (29:9).
All of you are standing today before the LORD your God— you leaders of tribes, elders, officials, and all the men of Israel, (29:10).
your children and wives, and the foreigners in your camps who cut your wood and draw your water— (29:11).
so that you may enter into the covenant of the LORD your God, which He is making with you today, and into His oath, (29:12).
and so that He may establish you today as His people, and He may be your God as He promised you and as He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. (29:13).
I am making this covenant and this oath not only with you, (29:14).
but also with those who are standing here with us today in the presence of the LORD our God, as well as with those who are not here today. (29:15).
For you yourselves know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the nations on the way here. (29:16).
You saw the abominations and idols among them made of wood and stone, of silver and gold. (29:17).

Make sure there is no man or woman, clan or tribe among you today whose heart turns away from the LORD our God to go and worship the gods of those nations. Make sure there is no root among you that bears such poisonous and bitter fruit, (29:18).

because when such a person hears the words of this oath, he invokes a blessing on himself, saying, ‘I will have peace, even though I walk in the stubbornness of my own heart.’ This will bring disaster on the watered land as well as the dry. (29:19).

The LORD will never be willing to forgive him. Instead, His anger and jealousy will burn against that man, and every curse written in this book will fall upon him. The LORD will blot out his name from under heaven (29:20).
and single him out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this Book of the Law. (29:21).
Then the generation to come — your sons who follow you and the foreigner who comes from a distant land — will see the plagues of the land and the sicknesses the LORD has inflicted on it. (29:22).

All its soil will be a burning waste of sulfur and salt, unsown and unproductive, with no plant growing on it, just like the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in His fierce anger. (29:23).
So all the nations will ask, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land? Why this great outburst of anger?’ (29:24).
And the people will answer, ‘It is because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers, which He made with them when He brought them out of the land of Egypt. (29:25).
They went and served other gods, and they worshiped gods they had not known— gods that the LORD had not given to them. (29:26).
Therefore the anger of the LORD burned against this land, and He brought upon it every curse written in this book. (29:27).
The LORD uprooted them from their land in His anger, rage, and great wrath, and He cast them into another land, where they are today.’ (29:28).
The secret things belong to the LORD our God, but the things revealed belong to us and to our children forever, so that we may follow all the words of this law. (29:29).
crossRefs: Joshua 24:14-27: Joshua puts the same choice to Israel at Shechem and sets up a stone as a witness against them.
Deuteronomy 8:4: Your clothing did not wear out and your feet did not swell during these forty years.
Genesis 19:24-25: The overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, the picture used in 29:23.
Hebrews 12:15: See that no bitter root grows up to cause trouble and defile many, an echo of 29:18.
Jeremiah 22:8-9: Nations passing by the ruined city will ask why the LORD did this, and the answer will be given.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָרַר (ʾārar), Greek: καταράομαι (kataraomai), Aramaic: ארר (arar)
translationNotes.note: Invocation of divine judgment on disobedience; contrasted with blessing.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בְּרִית (berit, 'covenant') - אָלָה (alah, 'sworn curse')
translationNotes.note: Two different legal instruments named together in 29:12 and 29:14. Berit is the agreement itself. Alah is the self-curse a party calls down on his own head if he breaks it, which is why 29:19 pictures a man hearing 'the words of this oath' and telling himself he will be fine anyway. Entering the covenant means accepting the curse attached to it.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חֹטֵב עֵצֶיךָ ... שֹׁאֵב מֵימֶיךָ (chotev etsekha ... shoev meymekha)
translationNotes.note: The lowest standing labor in the camp, and the phrase names a class, not two jobs. Joshua assigns exactly this status to the Gibeonites after their deception (Joshua 9:21-27). Listing them in 29:11 makes the point of the muster: the covenant is being sworn by leaders and by the foreign laborer at the bottom of the camp alike.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אַדְמָה (Admah) - צְבוֹיִם (Tsevoyim)
translationNotes.note: Two more cities of the plain, usually forgotten because Sodom and Gomorrah are remembered. All four appear as separate kingdoms with named kings in Genesis 14:2. Naming the full set here makes the warning concrete: a whole cluster of settled cities went to salt and sulfur together.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses recounts Israel's wilderness experience and calls them to follow the covenant terms, warning that anyone who turns to worship other gods will face God's wrath, curses, and exile; future generations will see the land become desolate like Sodom and understand it happened because Israel abandoned the LORD.

stories.title: ⛰️ Deuteronomy 30
summaryBullets: “When all these things come upon you— the blessings and curses I have set before you— and you call them to mind in all the nations to which the LORD your God has banished you, (30:1).
and when you and your children return to the LORD your God and obey His voice with all your heart and all your soul according to everything I am giving you today, (30:2).
then He will restore you from captivity and have compassion on you and gather you from all the nations to which the LORD your God has scattered you. (30:3).
Even if you have been banished to the farthest horizon, He will gather you and return you from there. (30:4).
And the LORD your God will bring you into the land your fathers possessed, and you will take possession of it. He will cause you to prosper and multiply more than your fathers. (30:5).
The LORD your God will circumcise your hearts and the hearts of your descendants, and you will love Him with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live. (30:6).
Then the LORD your God will put all these curses upon your enemies who hate you and persecute you. (30:7).
And you will again obey the voice of the LORD and follow all His commandments I am giving you today. (30:8).

So the LORD your God will make you abound in all the work of your hands and in the fruit of your womb, the offspring of your livestock, and the produce of your land. Indeed, the LORD will again delight in your prosperity, as He delighted in that of your fathers, (30:9).
if you obey the LORD your God by keeping His commandments and statutes that are written in this Book of the Law, and if you turn to Him with all your heart and with all your soul. (30:10).
For this commandment I give you today is not too difficult for you or beyond your reach. (30:11).
It is not in heaven, that you should need to ask, ‘Who will ascend into heaven to get it for us and proclaim it, that we may obey it?’ (30:12).
And it is not beyond the sea, that you should need to ask, ‘Who will cross the sea to get it for us and proclaim it, that we may obey it?’ (30:13).
But the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you may obey it. (30:14).
See, I have set before you today life and prosperity, as well as death and disaster. (30:15).

For I am commanding you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments, statutes, and ordinances, so that you may live and increase, and the LORD your God may bless you in the land that you are entering to possess. (30:16).
But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, but are drawn away to bow down to other gods and worship them, (30:17).
I declare to you today that you will surely perish; you shall not prolong your days in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess. (30:18).
I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing. Therefore choose life, so that you and your descendants may live, (30:19).

and that you may love the LORD your God, obey Him, and hold fast to Him. For He is your life, and He will prolong your life in the land that the LORD swore to give to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” (30:20).
crossRefs: Romans 10:6-8: Paul quotes this chapter, that the word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart.
Deuteronomy 10:16: Circumcise your hearts and stiffen your necks no longer, the command this promise answers.
Jeremiah 31:31-34: A new covenant, with the law put within them and written on their hearts.
Ezekiel 36:24-28: God gathers them from the nations, gives them a new heart, and puts His Spirit within them.
Nehemiah 1:8-9: Nehemiah prays back this exact promise: if you return to Me, I will gather you from the farthest horizon.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מוּל אֶת־לְבָב (mul et-levav), Greek: περιτέμνω τὴν καρδίαν (peritemnō tēn kardian), Aramaic: מולי לבא (mule liba)
translationNotes.note: Spiritual renewal removing hardness of heart so one loves God.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וְשָׁב ... אֶת־שְׁבוּתְךָ (ve-shav ... et shevutekha)
translationNotes.note: The verb shuv, to turn or return, runs through the whole chapter and English cannot hold it together. The people turn back to God (30:2), God turns their turning (30:3), and He turns again to delight in them (30:9). The phrase in 30:3 is a play on its own words: He will turn your turning.

translationNotes.term: Not in heaven, nor beyond the sea
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא ... וְלֹא־מֵעֵבֶר לַיָּם (lo va-shamayim hi ... ve-lo me-ever la-yam)
translationNotes.note: The two standard images for the unreachable in that world: straight up and out past the horizon of the water. Moses uses the pair to say the command needs no expedition and no expert to fetch it, because it has already been spoken aloud to them and is in their mouths.

translationNotes.term: I call heaven and earth as witnesses
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הַעִידֹתִי בָכֶם ... אֶת־הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת־הָאָרֶץ (ha'idoti vakhem ... et ha-shamayim ve-et ha-arets)
translationNotes.note: A formal witness clause. Treaties of that world listed the gods of both parties as witnesses to the terms; Deuteronomy calls heaven and earth instead, the two things that outlast every generation who could testify. The same summons opens the prophets' lawsuits (Isaiah 1:2, Micah 6:1-2) and closes this book at 31:28 and 32:1.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses promises that if Israel repents and returns to God, he will restore them from exile, prosper them, and circumcise their hearts; he sets before them the choice between life and death, commanding obedience to God's commands and warning that turning to other gods will bring destruction.

headings.text: The Choice of Life or Death

stories.title: 🙏 Deuteronomy 31
summaryBullets: When Moses had finished speaking these words to all Israel, (31:1).
he said to them, “I am now a hundred and twenty years old; I am no longer able to come and go, and the LORD has said to me, ‘You shall not cross the Jordan.’ (31:2).
The LORD your God Himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will dispossess them. Joshua will cross ahead of you, as the LORD has said. (31:3).
And the LORD will do to them as He did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, when He destroyed them along with their land. (31:4).
The LORD will deliver them over to you, and you must do to them exactly as I have commanded you. (31:5).
Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid or terrified of them, for it is the LORD your God who goes with you; He will never leave you nor forsake you.” (31:6).

Then Moses called for Joshua and said to him in the presence of all Israel, “Be strong and courageous, for you will go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their fathers to give them, and you shall give it to them as an inheritance. (31:7).
The LORD Himself goes before you; He will be with you. He will never leave you nor forsake you. Do not be afraid or discouraged.” (31:8).
So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel. (31:9).
Then Moses commanded them, “At the end of every seven years, at the appointed time in the year of remission of debt, during the Feast of Tabernacles, (31:10).
when all Israel comes before the LORD your God at the place He will choose, you are to read this law in the hearing of all Israel. (31:11).

Assemble the people— men, women, children, and the foreigners within your gates— so that they may listen and learn to fear the LORD your God and to follow carefully all the words of this law. (31:12).
Then their children who do not know the law will listen and learn to fear the LORD your God, as long as you live in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.” (31:13).

Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, the time of your death is near. Call Joshua and present yourselves at the Tent of Meeting, so that I may commission him.” So Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves at the Tent of Meeting. (31:14).
Then the LORD appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the cloud stood over the entrance to the tent. (31:15).

And the LORD said to Moses, “You will soon rest with your fathers, and these people will rise up and prostitute themselves with the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will forsake Me and break the covenant I have made with them. (31:16).

On that day My anger will burn against them, and I will abandon them and hide My face from them, so that they will be consumed, and many troubles and afflictions will befall them. On that day they will say, ‘Have not these disasters come upon us because our God is no longer with us?’ (31:17).
And on that day I will surely hide My face because of all the evil they have done by turning to other gods. (31:18).
Now therefore, write down for yourselves this song and teach it to the Israelites; have them recite it, so that it may be a witness for Me against them. (31:19).

When I have brought them into the land that I swore to give their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey, they will eat their fill and prosper. Then they will turn to other gods and worship them, and they will reject Me and break My covenant. (31:20).

And when many troubles and afflictions have come upon them, this song will testify against them, because it will not be forgotten from the lips of their descendants. For I know their inclination, even before I bring them into the land that I swore to give them.” (31:21).
So that very day Moses wrote down this song and taught it to the Israelites. (31:22).
Then the LORD commissioned Joshua son of Nun and said, “Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the Israelites into the land that I swore to give them, and I will be with you.” (31:23).
When Moses had finished writing in a book the words of this law from beginning to end, (31:24).
he gave this command to the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD: (31:25).
“Take this Book of the Law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, so that it may remain there as a witness against you. (31:26).
For I know how rebellious and stiff-necked you are. If you are already rebelling against the LORD while I am still alive, how much more will you rebel after my death! (31:27).
Assemble before me all the elders of your tribes and all your officers so that I may speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth to witness against them. (31:28).

For I know that after my death you will become utterly corrupt and turn from the path I have commanded you. And in the days to come, disaster will befall you because you will do evil in the sight of the LORD to provoke Him to anger by the work of your hands.” (31:29).
Then Moses recited aloud to the whole assembly of Israel the words of this song from beginning to end: (31:30).
crossRefs: Joshua 1:1-9: Joshua is told three times to be strong and courageous, for the LORD will not leave him nor forsake him.
Numbers 27:18-23: Joshua is set before Eleazar and the whole assembly and commissioned by the laying on of hands.
Deuteronomy 32:1-43: The song Moses writes here and teaches as a witness against Israel.
Nehemiah 8:13-18: The people find this law at the Feast of Booths, build shelters, and hear it read every day.
2 Kings 22:8-13: The Book of the Law is found in the temple and read to Josiah, who tears his clothes.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: סִיחֹן (Sichon) - Hebrew: עוֹג (Og)
translationNotes.note: The two Amorite kings east of the Jordan, and the only campaign this generation had actually won. Sihon ruled Heshbon and refused Israel passage on the King's Highway; Og ruled Bashan, the high grazing plateau north-east of the Sea of Galilee, from Ashtaroth and Edrei (Numbers 21:21-35). Deuteronomy 3:11 notes that Og's iron bedstead, nine cubits long, was still on show in Rabbah of the Ammonites.

translationNotes.term: The year of remission, at the Feast of Tabernacles
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׁמִטָּה (shemittah) - Hebrew: סֻכּוֹת (Sukkot)
translationNotes.note: Every seventh year the fields were left unworked (Leviticus 25:1-7) and outstanding debts were released (Deuteronomy 15:1-2). Tabernacles fell in the seventh month, five days after the Day of Atonement, and ran seven days with the whole nation living in booths made of branches (Leviticus 23:33-43). Verses 10 to 13 schedule the public reading of the law for the one week when nobody was in the fields and everyone, including women, children, and resident foreigners, was already assembled.

translationNotes.term: The Tent of Meeting and the pillar of cloud
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד (ohel moed)
translationNotes.note: Moed means an appointed meeting, so the name is the tent of appointment, the fixed place where God met Moses. Exodus 33:7-11 describes the arrangement: Moses went out to the tent, the people stood at their own tent doors and watched, the pillar of cloud came down and stood at the entrance, and the LORD spoke there. Verse 15 has that same cloud standing at the door for Joshua's commissioning.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: זָנָה (zanah)
translationNotes.note: Zanah is the ordinary verb for sexual immorality, and the prophets use it for covenant unfaithfulness without softening it, because in practice the two ran together. Numbers 25:1-3 records what verse 16 predicts: Israelite men joined themselves to Baal of Peor through the women of Moab, ate the sacrifices, and bowed to their gods.

translationNotes.term: Placed beside the ark as a witness
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לְעֵד (le-ed)
translationNotes.note: A treaty in the ancient Near East was written out, deposited in a sanctuary, and read aloud in public at set intervals, and the surviving Hittite treaties of the second millennium BC carry both requirements in their own texts. Verses 24 to 26 do the same three things with this law: written to the end, handed to the Levites who carry the ark, and lodged beside it so it stands as testimony that cannot be denied later.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses tells Israel he cannot cross the Jordan and commissions Joshua to lead them; he writes down the law for the Levites to read every seven years and composes a song as a witness against Israel's future unfaithfulness, which the Lord says will come when they prosper in the promised land.

headings.text: The Law Placed in the Ark

stories.title: 🙏 Deuteronomy 32
summaryBullets: Give ear, O heavens, and I will speak; hear, O earth, the words of my mouth. (32:1).
Let my teaching fall like rain and my speech settle like dew, like gentle rain on new grass, like showers on tender plants. (32:2).
For I will proclaim the name of the LORD. Ascribe greatness to our God! (32:3).
He is the Rock, His work is perfect; all His ways are just. A God of faithfulness without injustice, righteous and upright is He. (32:4).
